messages.content:
You answer questions for an engineering team from a memory store. The user message holds the memory you may use, then the question.
Rules:
- Answer only from the memory provided. Do not use outside knowledge and do not guess.
- If the memory does not contain the answer, reply exactly: I don't know
- When the memory does contain it, reply in one short line with just the value asked for (a name, a team, a service, a date, a note label, a reason) and nothing else.
- When a value changed over time, answer for the moment the question asks about; without a stated moment, answer for now. Today is 2026-06-30.
- Memory entries carry the date they were recorded. Treat a later entry as superseding an earlier one on the same subject.

Memory:
- [2025-10-27] incident-review/INC-2025-023: Review of INC-2025-023 (the search indexer, 2025-10-24). The root cause was a reindex job that failed silently on a full disk. We decided that reindex jobs will page on failure, because a silent reindex failure left stale results for two days in INC-2025-023.
- [2025-11-07] standup/boreal/2025-11-07: We agreed today that search-indexer will rebuild the index nightly instead of on every catalog write. The reason is that incremental updates left stale entries behind after failed writes.
- [2025-08-13] standup/boreal/2025-08-13: The search indexer must stay on OpenSearch 2.11 until the full reindex completes. Reminder that reporting depends on the ledger.
- [2025-04-18] incident-review/INC-2025-011: Incident review INC-2025-011. Ledger saw write latency spike tenfold for an hour on 2025-04-13. Root cause: an index missing after the schema migration. Decision: ledger migrations will ship with a reviewed query plan, because a missing index after a migration caused INC-2025-011.
- [2025-05-30] standup/atlas/2025-05-30: The ledger is pinned to Postgres 14; the pin lifts when the partitioning work finishes.
- [2025-08-29] standup/cinder/2025-08-29-2: The Cinder team noticed that search-indexer's disk usage jumped 30 percent after the retention change and pinged the owners.
- [2026-05-22] incident-review/INC-2026-009: Incident review INC-2026-009. The scheduler ran the nightly jobs twice on 2026-05-16. Root cause: two leaders elected during a network partition. Decision: the scheduler leader lease will be shortened to ten seconds, because two leaders ran the nightly jobs twice in INC-2026-009.
- [2025-12-15] handover/2025-12-15-search-indexer-correction: The 2025-11-18 note about the indexer named the wrong team. The Dune team took it over on that date; the Ember team did not.
- [2025-03-06] incident-review/INC-2025-004: INC-2025-004 review. What happened: notifier missed alerts for 40 minutes on 2025-03-04. Why: a consumer offset stuck after a broker restart. Follow-up decision: notifier consumers will commit offsets every five seconds, because a stuck offset went unnoticed for 40 minutes during INC-2025-004.
- [2026-03-16] standup/ember/2026-03-16: Oskar has the Ember pager this cycle, taking over from Diego Alvarez. Ember noticed that search-indexer's queue depth hit 50,000 after the marketing send and pinged the owners.
- [2025-08-20] standup/cinder/2025-08-20: Decision: clients will cache feature-flags evaluations for 30 seconds, because feature-flags saw 40,000 requests per second at peak and most of them were identical. Cinder noticed that the reporting service's p99 latency doubled after Tuesday's deploy and pinged the owners.
- [2025-11-11] standup/atlas/2025-11-11: Deploy freeze for billing-api: 2025-11-24 to 2025-12-02 (the peak season). Observation from the Atlas team: after Tuesday's deploy, search-indexer's p99 latency doubled.
- [2025-03-31] standup/boreal/2025-03-31-2: We agreed today that the notifier will retry failed pushes three times with exponential backoff. The reason is that the flat one-second retry was hammering the push provider during its outages.
- [2025-09-15] standup/boreal/2025-09-15-2: Team Boreal still owns search-indexer, in case anyone asks.
- [2025-06-06] standup/boreal/2025-06-06: Boreal saw that the reports pipeline's disk usage jumped 30 percent following the retention change; not their service, so they flagged it.
- [2025-08-08] standup/dune/2025-08-08: New deploy window for the job scheduler: on weekdays between 08:00 and 10:00 UTC, never on Fridays. Forget the previous Tuesdays 13:00-15:00 UTC slot. Observation from the Dune team: after the marketing send, billing-api's queue depth hit 50,000.
- [2026-04-16] standup/atlas/2026-04-16: Team Atlas saw that the billing service's error rate crept up to 2 percent following the dependency bump; not their service, so they flagged it.
- [2026-04-16] standup/atlas/2026-04-16-2: Atlas saw that Ledger's disk usage jumped 30 percent following the retention change; not their service, so they flagged it. Atlas planning meeting is every Tuesday.
- [2025-03-28] standup/ember/2025-03-28: If feature-flags is down, the job scheduler is down: it relies on it for per-job kill switches.
- [2025-04-01] standup/cinder/2025-04-01: We agreed today that the catalog will keep image metadata in a separate table. The reason is that the joined writes were locking product updates for seconds at a time.
- [2025-09-19] standup/boreal/2025-09-19: We decided that reporting will read from the event-bus instead of querying the ledger directly. The reason: the nightly ledger scans were blocking billing runs. That removes the dependency on Ledger from the reporting service.
